correctness.rationale: The proof reconstructs the exact distance-difference values for same-part and cross-part pairs, exhausts support sizes one, two, and at least three, and derives minima and basis counts from that characterization. Direct exhaustive enumeration on all 58 complete multipartite types through order 8 matched the characterization, minimum formula, and basis-count formula on every case.

originality.rationale: The complete-bipartite cases are explicitly prior work. Acceptance-time published-finding corpus searches for complete-multipartite doubly resolving sets, double metric dimension, all-set characterizations, and exact formulas returned no equivalent or stronger result. The later lexicographic-product literature is conservatively treated as possible overlap for balanced subclasses, leaving the arbitrary unequal-part all-set classification and basis counts as the novelty basis.

value.rationale: The theorem characterizes every doubly resolving set of an arbitrary complete multipartite graph and converts the structural criterion into exact values and exact counts of minimum sets, exposing the role of singleton and size-two parts in a reusable closed form.
